narrative.northStar: The Technical Manual You Can Run
narrative.overview:
The classroom is printed like a two-color engineering manual. White pages sit on a cool light-table ground; the text is press black; one spot ink marks each part of the library, with a house ultramarine for the catalog and the interface. Every subject is a thumb-indexed part, and every lesson is a spread: the chapter on the left page, a runnable listing and its printed result on the right. Learners read, predict, run and read the result without losing their place.

Density is that of a reference book, not a marketing site: hairline rules, tabular folio numerals and compact 4px controls carry the structure. Code and output are set on dark slate, like listings in a printed manual, so they read as a different material from the prose. The interface speaks in the system grotesque; chapters speak in Latin Modern, the typeface of a typeset textbook.

The world deliberately refuses the course-platform card grid with progress rings, gradient heroes and decorative glass.
keyCharacteristics: Two inks per surface: press black plus one spot ink (house ultramarine or a subject area's ink).
Pages, not cards: hairline rules and 3px part rules divide content.
Tabular numerals for folios, counts and timings.
Dark slate listings and results under light pages.
Latin Modern chapters, system grotesque interface.

rules.name: The One Spot Ink Rule
rules.body: A surface uses press black plus exactly one spot ink: house ultramarine on the catalog and interface, or the current subject's ink on its part. Two spot inks never compete on one surface.

rules.name: The Color Is Never Alone Rule
rules.body: Every subject ink travels with a text label (thumb tab text, part heading, subject name), so color never carries meaning by itself.

rules.name: The Doing and Reading Rule
rules.body: Anything you operate is set in the grotesque; anything you study is set in Latin Modern. Never set a control in the serif or a chapter paragraph in the grotesque.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Folios, counts, timings and progress use tabular numerals so columns of numbers align like a printed index.

rules.name: The Paper Not Glass Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are opaque paper. No blur, no translucency, no glow; a floating dialog earns the lift shadow and nothing more.

dos: **Do** keep each surface to press black plus one spot ink (The One Spot Ink Rule).
**Do** pair every subject ink with its text label.
**Do** set chapters in Latin Modern at 1.0625rem/1.75 within 78ch, and interface text in the system grotesque.
**Do** use tabular numerals for folios, counts, timings and progress.
**Do** print run output on listing slate directly under the run controls, unwrapped.
**Do** keep controls at 4px corners and 40px minimum height, panels at 8px.
donts: **Don't** build uniform card grids, progress rings or gradient heroes; the home page is a contents page.
**Don't** add eyebrow or kicker labels above headings.
**Don't** use colored side borders thicker than 1px on cards or callouts.
**Don't** use blur, translucency or glow (The Paper Not Glass Rule).
**Don't** let two subject inks share one surface.
